FLASHCARD SET · AGES 4–5 YEARS

Phonics & Beginning Sounds flashcards.

Twenty-six cards, one for every letter: big Aa beside the apple, Bb beside the ball, all the way to Zz beside the zebra. Every card carries its picture word, its sound script for grown-ups and one tiny activity — the whole alphabet’s worth of first sounds, ready to print.

These cards belong to Class 28 · Phonics & Beginning Sounds on the Kiddo School learning path.

Every card in the set.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    Play the sound hunt

    Pick one card, then hunt the house for three things that start with its sound. The apple card finds an apron, an avocado, an animal toy — three finds and the sound is owned.

  2. 02

    Say the sounds, not the names

    Line the cards up and sing the alphabet in sounds instead of letter names: a-a-apple, b-b-ball. It is the same song the reading books speak.

  3. 03

    Play the mismatch game

    Hold up the moon card and say "m — m — marble!" — a deliberate mistake. Children correct grown-ups with enormous joy, and correcting is the drill.

  4. 04

    Trace the big letters

    Finger-trace the big Aa while saying its sound out loud. Eyes, mouth and fingertip all hold the same letter at once — that is how sounds stick.

      Apple Flashcard — Letter A for Preschoolers

      Big navy letters Aa beside a shiny red apple — the card that opens the set, because apple is a word every child already owns and its first sound is the clearest /a/ there is.

      How this card helps

      The pair Aa sits beside the apple in one look, so the letter shape and its sound arrive together instead of as two separate school facts to memorise.

      How to use this card

      Be the echo: the grown-up says “a — a — apple” and the child echoes it back three times, getting a little quieter each time until it is a whisper. Whispers force careful listening.

      What kids learn from it

      That letters are pictures of sounds: this shape Aa stands for the first mouth-sound of apple — the idea every later reading skill is built on.

      Print it like this

      Print landscape on A4 or Letter at 100% — the Aa card keeps its full 2000×1414 frame. Slide it into a clear sleeve and it survives breakfast.

      How to teach with this card

      Ask for the sound, never “what letter is this?” — “what sound?” keeps the child’s ear in charge, and the ear is what reading runs on.

      Letter sound

      A makes its short sound /a/ — the wide-open “ah” that starts apple, ant and alligator. Mouth open wide, tongue low: the biggest mouth-shape of all the letters.

      Teach it, step by step

      Ball Flashcard — Letter B for Preschoolers

      Bb beside a bright beach ball — the /b/ sound is a lip-pop, and ball is usually one of the first words a child says, which makes this card an easy win.

      How this card helps

      The letter pair Bb sits beside the ball, so the shape and its pop-sound arrive in one look — and because /b/ is visibly made with the lips, children can watch themselves say it.

      How to use this card

      Play bounce-and-say: one bounce, one b-word. Ball, bounce, big, blue, bunny — when the b-words run out, start the round again faster.

      What kids learn from it

      That Bb is a lip-pop sound with the voice buzzing — and that the same sound can start a whole family of words, not just one.

      Print it like this

      Print landscape on A4 or Letter at 100%; the Bb card keeps its full 2000×1414 frame. Print two and the pair makes a matching game.

      How to teach with this card

      Let your child feel the /b/ by touching their own lips — sounds a child can feel are sounds a child remembers.

      Letter sound

      B makes the /b/ sound — lips pressed together, then popped open with the voice on. It is the first sound of ball, bat and bubble.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Ball lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Phonics & Beginning Sounds (Class 28) class on the Learning Path.

      Cat Flashcard — Letter C for Preschoolers

      Cc beside a smiling orange tabby — cat is the classic first c-word for good reason: the /c/ here is a clean, short /k/ that children can hear and say from toddler age.

      How this card helps

      Cc next to the cat ties the letter shape to the /k/ click — a sound made at the very back of the mouth, so the card teaches listening as much as looking.

      How to use this card

      Play the clicking cat: every time the grown-up says a c-word, the child answers with one cat meow. Five c-words, five meows, lots of giggles.

      What kids learn from it

      That the same shape Cc can carry the /k/ sound at the start of cat, cup and car — one sound, many words, one card to hold them.

      Print it like this

      Print landscape on A4 or Letter at 100% — the Cc card keeps its full 2000×1414 frame and its colours survive a home printer well.

      How to teach with this card

      If your child confuses c and k later, that is normal — they make the identical sound. Tell them they are twins with two coats.

      Letter sound

      C makes the /k/ sound in cat — a clean click at the back of the mouth, like a tiny door shutting: cat, cup, car, cake.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Cat lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Phonics & Beginning Sounds (Class 28) class on the Learning Path.

      Dog Flashcard — Letter D for Preschoolers

      Dd beside a smiling golden puppy — dog is the d-word nearly every child can say, and the /d/ tap of the tongue behind the teeth is easy to feel.

      How this card helps

      The letter pair Dd beside the puppy links the shape to the tongue-tap — and the tapping motion gives the sound a body movement to stick to.

      How to use this card

      March like a dog around the room and give one bark per d-word the grown-up calls: dog, duck, dad, door. Wrong word, no bark — that is the game.

      What kids learn from it

      That Dd carries the /d/ tap at the start of dog and dad — and that feeling where the tongue taps is as useful as seeing the letter.

      Print it like this

      Print landscape on A4 or Letter at 100%; the Dd card keeps its full 2000×1414 frame. Sleeve it — dog cards get carried around.

      How to teach with this card

      Say d-d-d-dog with four bounces before saying the word — the repeated onset makes the target sound impossible to miss.

      Letter sound

      D makes the /d/ sound — a quick tongue-tap behind the top teeth with the voice on: dog, dad, duck, door.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Dog lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Phonics & Beginning Sounds (Class 28) class on the Learning Path.

      Elephant Flashcard — Letter E for Preschoolers

      Ee beside a smiling grey elephant — the elephant word is long, but its first sound is the short /e/, and an elephant is exactly the kind of animal children will happily say over and over.

      How this card helps

      The letter pair Ee beside the elephant anchors the short /e/ — and because elephant is a long word, children hear the /e/ burst right at its start every single time.

      How to use this card

      Be the elephant echo: grown-up says “e — e — elephant”, child swings their trunk and echoes it. Then swap roles — being the teacher cements the sound.

      What kids learn from it

      That Ee is the “eh” vowel of elephant, egg and elf — and that the same vowel can open a little word like egg and a big one like elephant.

      Print it like this

      Print landscape on A4 or Letter at 100% — the Ee card keeps its full 2000×1414 frame, and the word box stays crisp at any size.

      How to teach with this card

      Stretch the first sound when the word is long: “eh — eh — eh-le-phant”. Slow starts teach the sound; fast finishes teach the word.

      Letter sound

      E makes its short sound /e/ — a relaxed “eh” that starts elephant, egg and elf. Mouth half open, flat tongue: the middle-mouth vowel.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Elephant lesson on the Learning Path.

      Fish Flashcard — Letter F for Preschoolers

      Ff beside a smiling teal fish — the /f/ is a windy sound made with lips and teeth, and fish is the animal most children meet first at dinner time or in the bath.

      How this card helps

      Ff beside the fish pairs the letter with the teeth-on-lip wind — a sound children can see in a mirror, which makes it one of the easiest to self-check.

      How to use this card

      Blow the fish across the table: cut a paper fish, race it with f-f-f puffs, and shout a f-word each time it lands — fish, fast, fin, done.

      What kids learn from it

      That Ff is a windy, voiceless sound made with teeth and lip — and that the same puff starts fish, frog and fork.

      Print it like this

      Print landscape on A4 or Letter at 100%; the Ff card keeps its full 2000×1414 frame and prints fast — lots of ink-free cream background.

      How to teach with this card

      Mirror work is gold here: if your child can see their top teeth touching their lip, they are making a true /f/.

      Letter sound

      F makes the /f/ sound — top teeth gently on the bottom lip, air blown through with no voice: fish, frog, fork, four.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Fish lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Phonics & Beginning Sounds (Class 28) class on the Learning Path.

      Goat Flashcard — Letter G for Preschoolers

      Gg beside a white goat with little horns — goat gives the hard /g/, a throat sound children love to make, and the goat’s silly face keeps them saying it.

      How this card helps

      Gg beside the goat anchors the hard /g/ — a sound made so far back that children feel it in their throat, which makes the card a body lesson too.

      How to use this card

      Play the goat game: butt an imaginary ball with your head while saying g-words — goat, go, giggle, again. Every head-butt earns a new word.

      What kids learn from it

      That Gg can carry the growly /g/ of goat and game — and that the same letter will one day wear a different sound, which is a normal thing letters do.

      Print it like this

      Print landscape on A4 or Letter at 100% — the Gg card keeps its full 2000×1414 frame, and the goat’s horns stay sharp even at half size.

      How to teach with this card

      If /g/ and /k/ get swapped, use the throat test: hand on the throat, /g/ buzzes, /k/ does not. The buzz is the whole difference.

      Letter sound

      G makes the hard /g/ sound — the back of the tongue lifts and lets go with the voice on: goat, game, gate, giggle.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Goat lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Phonics & Beginning Sounds (Class 28) class on the Learning Path.

      Hat Flashcard — Letter H for Preschoolers

      Hh beside a blue hat with a red band — /h/ is just a breath, which makes it the easiest sound to whisper and the one children most often drop from words.

      How this card helps

      Hh beside the hat attaches the letter to the breath itself — /h/ has no mouth shape to copy, so the picture word does the anchoring.

      How to use this card

      Play the h-breath races: huff like the big bad wolf at an imaginary door — h-h-h-hat — then walk in and name three hats you can see in the room.

      What kids learn from it

      That Hh is a breath with a letter on it — and that adding one small puff at the front turns “at” into “hat”, a magic trick children adore.

      Print it like this

      Print landscape on A4 or Letter at 100%; the Hh card keeps its full 2000×1414 frame and the red band keeps its colour at low ink.

      How to teach with this card

      Whisper /h/ on purpose — the sound is nearly silent, so whispering it makes children listen hard, and hard listening is the skill.

      Letter sound

      H makes the /h/ sound — a gentle breath out, no shape and no voice, like fogging a window: hat, hand, house, hello.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Hat lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Phonics & Beginning Sounds (Class 28) class on the Learning Path.

      Igloo Flashcard — Letter I for Preschoolers

      Ii beside a snowy igloo — igloo is the classic short-i picture word, and the /i/ “ih” is a tiny, tight sound that sits between e and u on the shelf.

      How this card helps

      Ii beside the igloo fixes the short /i/ — a sound so small children tend to skip it, and the igloo gives it a picture worth pointing at.

      How to use this card

      Build an igloo of cushions, crawl inside and whisper i-words — igloo, in, it — because a sound this small sounds best in a small space.

      What kids learn from it

      That Ii carries the quick “ih” of igloo and insect — and that vowels are the sounds the voice sings, even when they are tiny.

      Print it like this

      Print landscape on A4 or Letter at 100% — the Ii card keeps its full 2000×1414 frame, and the pale igloo survives grayscale printing nicely.

      How to teach with this card

      If “igloo” keeps coming out “eegloo”, say “ih — ih — igloo” with three tight starts; the repetition resets the vowel.

      Letter sound

      I makes its short sound /i/ — a quick, tight “ih” that starts igloo, insect and in. Mouth barely open, tongue high and forward.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Igloo lesson on the Learning Path.

      Jam Flashcard — Letter J for Preschoolers

      Jj beside a strawberry jam jar — /j/ is a jump of the tongue with the voice on, and jam is the j-word children taste, not just say.

      How this card helps

      Jj beside the jam jar pairs the letter with the tongue-jump — a sound children can feel pop, and the sticky red jar makes the word unforgettable.

      How to use this card

      Jump for j: every j-word the grown-up calls earns one real jump — jam, jump, jog, jelly. The word is the springboard; the jump is the reward.

      What kids learn from it

      That Jj is the jumping sound at the start of jam, jump and juice — and that the letter looks like the motion: a hook that jumps down.

      Print it like this

      Print landscape on A4 or Letter at 100%; the Jj card keeps its full 2000×1414 frame, and the gingham lid prints crisply at any scale.

      How to teach with this card

      Pair j with its feel-alike: /j/ and /ch/ are made in the same spot, /j/ buzzes and /ch/ puffs — jam versus chin. One buzz, one puff.

      Letter sound

      J makes the /j/ sound — the tongue jumps from behind the teeth with the voice buzzing: jam, jump, juice, jet.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Jam lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Phonics & Beginning Sounds (Class 28) class on the Learning Path.

      Kite Flashcard — Letter K for Preschoolers

      Kk beside a colourful diamond kite — the /k/ click is identical to hard c, and kite is the word that shows it: same sound, new letter shape, still flying.

      How this card helps

      Kk beside the kite gives the /k/ click its own letter after cat showed it as c — two shapes, one sound, and the kite makes the second one friendly.

      How to use this card

      Kick-and-say: kick a soft ball gently across the room, one k-word per kick — kick, kite, key, kind. Miss the ball, say the word anyway.

      What kids learn from it

      That Kk says the same /k/ as c in cat — the big idea that sounds can wear different letter coats, which is half of all English spelling.

      Print it like this

      Print landscape on A4 or Letter at 100% — the Kk card keeps its full 2000×1414 frame, and the rainbow kite is the brightest thing on the shelf.

      How to teach with this card

      Say “c and k are twins” out loud with your child — naming the twin sounds early prevents the classic “which one?” spelling tears later.

      Letter sound

      K makes the /k/ sound — the same back-of-the-mouth click as cat, here in its own letter: kite, kick, key, kangaroo.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Kite lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Phonics & Beginning Sounds (Class 28) class on the Learning Path.

      Lion Flashcard — Letter L for Preschoolers

      Ll beside a golden lion with a great dark mane — /l/ is the singing tongue-tip sound, and the lion’s mane curls exactly like a lowercase l, which is a lesson all by itself.

      How this card helps

      Ll beside the lion pairs the letter with the lifting tongue — and the lion’s mane echoing the lowercase l gives children a picture-memory of the shape itself.

      How to use this card

      Roar and lift: one gentle roar per l-word — lion, lip, leg, love — with the tongue tip visibly up at every roar. Silly, loud, effective.

      What kids learn from it

      That Ll is the tongue-tip singing sound of lion and love — and that the lowercase l curls like the lion’s mane, so the shape has a story.

      Print it like this

      Print landscape on A4 or Letter at 100%; the Ll card keeps its full 2000×1414 frame and the golden mane survives every printer.

      How to teach with this card

      Hold the sound: /l/ can sing as long as there is breath — l-l-l-l-lion. Long sounds teach the mouth shape better than short bursts.

      Letter sound

      L makes the /l/ sound — tongue tip up behind the top teeth, voice on, air flowing around the sides: lion, lip, leg, love.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Lion lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Phonics & Beginning Sounds (Class 28) class on the Learning Path.

      Moon Flashcard — Letter M for Preschoolers

      Mm beside a smiling moon — /m/ is the humming lip sound children make before any word at all (“mmm”), which makes this the most rehearsed letter in the set.

      How this card helps

      Mm beside the moon anchors the humming sound — the easiest for children to feel and the first consonant most babies ever say.

      How to use this card

      Moon-hum lullaby: hum m-m-m to a slow tune, then swap the hum for m-words — moon, mum, milk — until the room is suitably sleepy.

      What kids learn from it

      That Mm is the humming sound made with the lips — and that m-words are everywhere a child already lives: mum, milk, moon, more.

      Print it like this

      Print landscape on A4 or Letter at 100% — the Mm card keeps its full 2000×1414 frame, and the smiling moon calms bedtime collections.

      How to teach with this card

      Close-lips test: if the lips are not touching, it is not /m/. One mirror check replaces ten corrections.

      Letter sound

      M makes the /m/ sound — lips together, voice humming through the nose: moon, mum, milk, more.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Moon lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Phonics & Beginning Sounds (Class 28) class on the Learning Path.

      Nest Flashcard — Letter N for Preschoolers

      Nn beside a nest with three pale eggs — /n/ is the nose-hum twin of /m/, and nest is the word that pairs it with a picture children want to protect.

      How this card helps

      Nn beside the nest attaches the letter to the nose-hum — and the three eggs give the card a counting bonus while the sound does its work.

      How to use this card

      Build a blanket nest, sit in it and take turns saying n-words — nest, night, nose, no. Saying “no” inside the nest is, for some reason, the best part.

      What kids learn from it

      That Nn hums through the nose with the tongue up — the twin of m with a different mouth, and the first sound of nest, nose and night.

      Print it like this

      Print landscape on A4 or Letter at 100%; the Nn card keeps its full 2000×1414 frame and the warm browns print well even in draft mode.

      How to teach with this card

      If n and m swap, slow the word down and touch nose then lips — the body keeps the two sounds sorted better than the ears do.

      Letter sound

      N makes the /n/ sound — tongue tip up behind the top teeth, voice humming through the nose: nest, nose, night, nine.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Nest lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Phonics & Beginning Sounds (Class 28) class on the Learning Path.

      Octopus Flashcard — Letter O for Preschoolers

      Oo beside a smiling purple octopus — octopus hands out the short /o/, the round “oh” that starts one of the few long words children will happily rehearse.

      How this card helps

      Oo beside the octopus fixes the round /o/ — and the octopus’s eight arms give you a free bonus: count them, one arm per o-word.

      How to use this card

      Eight-arm octopus: wiggle eight imaginary arms while saying o-words — one wiggle, one word: octopus, on, off, otter. Eight is harder than it sounds.

      What kids learn from it

      That Oo is the round vowel of octopus and on — and that the letter’s shape is the mouth shape, which is exactly why o is easy to teach first.

      Print it like this

      Print landscape on A4 or Letter at 100% — the Oo card keeps its full 2000×1414 frame, and the purple prints richly even on plain paper.

      How to teach with this card

      Draw the o in the air with one finger while saying the sound — the round shape, the round mouth and the round letter lock together.

      Letter sound

      O makes its short sound /o/ — a round “oh” that starts octopus, ox and on. Lips rounded like a little circle: the letter draws its own mouth shape.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Octopus lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Phonics & Beginning Sounds (Class 28) class on the Learning Path.

      Pig Flashcard — Letter P for Preschoolers

      Pp beside a smiling pink pig — /p/ is the puff twin of /b/, and pig is the p-word with the best snout: children snort first and say the sound second.

      How this card helps

      Pp beside the pig pairs the letter with the puff — and because /p/ is invisible inside the mouth, the tissue and mirror games do the teaching.

      How to use this card

      Snort-and-say: snort like a pig, then say a p-word — pig, pop, pink, park. Snort first, word second; the silliness carries the drilling.

      What kids learn from it

      That Pp is the puff sound of pig and pop — and that p and b are lip twins, which is a fact worth knowing the day spelling gets tricky.

      Print it like this

      Print landscape on A4 or Letter at 100%; the Pp card keeps its full 2000×1414 frame and the pink prints softly at low ink.

      How to teach with this card

      Exaggerate the puff — p-p-pig with a visible air-blast is far easier to copy than a careful quiet p.

      Letter sound

      P makes the /p/ sound — lips pressed together, then a little puff of air with no voice: pig, pop, park, pink.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Pig lesson on the Learning Path.

      Queen Flashcard — Letter Q for Preschoolers

      Qq beside a smiling queen — on this card q sounds like “kw”, two sounds in one letter, and the queen is the picture every preschooler already knows how to bow to.

      How this card helps

      Qq beside the queen teaches English’s only two-sound letter — /kw/ — and the crowned queen gives the sound a face children already respect.

      How to use this card

      Royal decrees: wear an imaginary crown, wave a sceptre and declare k-words royal — “Henceforth: queen! quick! quilt!”. Bow after each decree.

      What kids learn from it

      That Qq carries two sounds glued together, /k/ plus /w/ — and that q always brings its friend u, a spelling fact that explains nearly every q-word.

      Print it like this

      Print landscape on A4 or Letter at 100% — the Qq card keeps its full 2000×1414 frame, and the crown and gown print beautifully in colour.

      How to teach with this card

      Say /kw/ as one burst, not two separate sounds — “kwuh-een” fast becomes queen; slow, it falls apart.

      Letter sound

      Q makes the /kw/ sound — a /k/ click followed instantly by /w/: queen, quick, quiet, quilt.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Queen lesson on the Learning Path.

      Rabbit Flashcard — Letter R for Preschoolers

      Rr beside a grey rabbit with long ears — /r/ curls the tongue and never touches it, which makes rabbit the r-word children say best and the sound grown-ups explain worst.

      How this card helps

      Rr beside the rabbit anchors the curling sound — and because r is invisible in a mirror, the growl-trick and the rabbit do the visible work.

      How to use this card

      Hop and say: bunny-hop three hops per r-word — rabbit, run, red, rain. Ears up with two fingers on the head; the ears make the r better.

      What kids learn from it

      That Rr is the curling sound of rabbit and run — and that some sounds live where the eye cannot see, which is why listening games matter.

      Print it like this

      Print landscape on A4 or Letter at 100%; the Rr card keeps its full 2000×1414 frame and the soft grey prints gently at any quality.

      How to teach with this card

      Never say “roll your r” — English r does not roll. Growl softly instead: the growl places the tongue better than any instruction.

      Letter sound

      R makes the /r/ sound — tongue curled toward the roof of the mouth without touching: rabbit, run, rain, red.

      Teach it, step by step

      Sun Flashcard — Letter S for Preschoolers

      Ss beside a smiling yellow sun — /s/ is the long hiss children can hold for a whole breath, and sun is the s-word that starts every good morning.

      How this card helps

      Ss beside the sun attaches the letter to the hiss — the one sound a child can already hold for five seconds, which makes it the set’s easiest win.

      How to use this card

      Sunshine circle: arms up like rays, spin slowly while hissing s, then land on an s-word — sun, sock, six, star. Dizzy giggles guaranteed.

      What kids learn from it

      That Ss is the hissing sound of sun and snake — a sound that can stretch, shrink and land on a whole family of s-words.

      Print it like this

      Print landscape on A4 or Letter at 100% — the Ss card keeps its full 2000×1414 frame, and the smiling sun is the cheeriest card on the wall.

      How to teach with this card

      Play the long-hiss record: whoever hisses longest picks the next s-word. Competition does the repetition for you.

      Letter sound

      S makes the /s/ sound — teeth nearly closed, air hissing through, no voice: sun, sock, six, snake.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Sun lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Phonics & Beginning Sounds (Class 28) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · PHONICS & BEGINNING SOUNDS · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Turtle Flashcard — Letter T for Preschoolers

      Tt beside a smiling green turtle — /t/ is the whisper twin of /d/, a quick tongue tap, and turtle is the t-word that walks slowly enough for anyone to say.

      How this card helps

      Tt beside the turtle pairs the letter with the tap — the most frequent consonant tap in English, drilled here with the slowest animal in the set.

      How to use this card

      Turtle race: walk very slowly, one giant slow step per t-word — turtle, toe, ten, take. Last one to finish wins, exactly like a turtle.

      What kids learn from it

      That Tt is the quiet tap of turtle and toe — and that t and d are tongue-tap twins separated only by the voice.

      Print it like this

      Print landscape on A4 or Letter at 100%; the Tt card keeps its full 2000×1414 frame and the greens print fresh at any setting.

      How to teach with this card

      Alternate t-t-d-d-t-t-d-d with your child — feeling the voice switch between the twins teaches both sounds at once.

      Letter sound

      T makes the /t/ sound — a whispery tongue-tap behind the top teeth: turtle, toe, tree, ten.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Turtle lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Phonics & Beginning Sounds (Class 28) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · PHONICS & BEGINNING SOUNDS · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Umbrella Flashcard — Letter U for Preschoolers

      Uu beside a rainbow umbrella — umbrella gives the short /u/, the relaxed “uh” that lives in up and under, and the rainbow keeps the card bright on an otherwise grey sound.

      How this card helps

      Uu beside the umbrella fixes the short /u/ — the vaguest vowel sound in English, rescued by a picture children can name from any rainy day.

      How to use this card

      Open an imaginary umbrella with a big “uh — uh — umbrella!”, then walk around it while trading u-words: up, under, uncle, umbrella upsidedown.

      What kids learn from it

      That Uu carries the relaxed “uh” of umbrella and up — the sound English makes when the mouth is completely at rest.

      Print it like this

      Print landscape on A4 or Letter at 100% — the Uu card keeps its full 2000×1414 frame, and the rainbow stripes survive every printer.

      How to teach with this card

      If umbrella drifts to “oo-mbrella”, say “uh — uh — umbrella” with three flat starts; the flatness is the whole vowel.

      Letter sound

      U makes its short sound /u/ — the relaxed “uh” that starts umbrella, up and under. Mouth loose, nothing stretched: the resting vowel.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Umbrella lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Phonics & Beginning Sounds (Class 28) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · PHONICS & BEGINNING SOUNDS · AGES 4–5 YEARS

      Van Flashcard — Letter V for Preschoolers

      Vv beside a white van — /v/ is the buzzing twin of /f/, teeth on lip with the voice on, and van is the v-word children can drive around the carpet.

      How this card helps

      Vv beside the van teaches the voiced lip-teeth sound — and driving the van around the room gives the sound a motion to ride on.

      How to use this card

      Drive the van: steer an invisible wheel, beep the horn once per v-word — van, vet, violin, vegetable. Left turns require a v-word too.

      What kids learn from it

      That Vv is the buzzing teeth-lip sound of van and violin — the loud twin of f, and one of the sounds English borrows proudly.

      Print it like this

      Print landscape on A4 or Letter at 100%; the Vv card keeps its full 2000×1414 frame and the white van prints cleanly even in grayscale.

      How to teach with this card

      Say f-v-f-v in one breath — feeling the voice switch on and off is faster than any explanation of “voiced” and “voiceless”.

      Letter sound

      V makes the /v/ sound — top teeth on the bottom lip with the voice buzzing: van, vet, violin, five.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Van lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Phonics & Beginning Sounds (Class 28) class on the Learning Path.

      Whale Flashcard — Letter W for Preschoolers

      Ww beside a blue whale with a spout — /w/ rounds the lips into a tiny circle and slides open, and the whale’s spout draws the sound’s shape in the air.

      How this card helps

      Ww beside the whale anchors the lip-glide — and the spout gives the sound an up-and-out motion that children can act while saying it.

      How to use this card

      Whale spout race: crouch, rise slowly with hands as a spout, whoosh at the top and land on a w-word — whale, wave, water, wonderful.

      What kids learn from it

      That Ww is the rounded glide of whale and water — a sound that moves, which is why it pairs so well with water words.

      Print it like this

      Print landscape on A4 or Letter at 100% — the Ww card keeps its full 2000×1414 frame, and the deep blues print beautifully in colour.

      How to teach with this card

      Start from “oo” (as in moon) and open quickly — oo-uuh becomes wuh. The glide from oo is the whole secret of w.

      Letter sound

      W makes the /w/ sound — lips rounded small then gliding open with the voice on: whale, water, wave, wind.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Whale lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Phonics & Beginning Sounds (Class 28) class on the Learning Path.

      Xylophone Flashcard — Letter X for Preschoolers

      Xx beside a rainbow xylophone — the honest card of the set: here x sounds like /z/ at the start of xylophone, while x’s usual job is the /ks/ at the end of box and fox.

      How this card helps

      Xx beside the xylophone opens the truth about x — a letter with two jobs — and the rainbow bars make the strangest letter the prettiest card.

      How to use this card

      Box-the-sound: make a box with your arms on every /ks/ ending — box! fox! six! — then play one pretend xylophone note for the /z/ exception.

      What kids learn from it

      That x mostly says /ks/ at the end of words, and that letters can have rare second jobs — xylophone being the most famous one in English.

      Print it like this

      Print landscape on A4 or Letter at 100%; the Xx card keeps its full 2000×1414 frame and the rainbow bars print as the set’s brightest page.

      How to teach with this card

      Say “x is a finisher” — it loves the end of words (box, six). Starting words is its rare gig, and xylophone got the gig.

      Letter sound

      X has two jobs. At the end of words it says /ks/ — box, fox, six. On this card, at the start of xylophone, it borrows /z/. Both are true; both are x.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Xylophone lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Phonics & Beginning Sounds (Class 28) class on the Learning Path.

      Yo-Yo Flashcard — Letter Y for Preschoolers

      Yy beside a blue yo-yo — /y/ is the quick glide that launches yes and you, and the yo-yo is the only toy that is also two y-sounds in a row.

      How this card helps

      Yy beside the yo-yo teaches the gliding sound — and the toy’s up-down motion matches the sound’s own slide from consonant into vowel.

      How to use this card

      Yo-yo trick time: pretend to walk the dog, rock the cradle, go around the world — one y-word per trick: yes, yawn, yell, yarn.

      What kids learn from it

      That Yy launches yes and yo-yo with a glide — and that y has a second, vowel life at the ends of words, waiting for later lessons.

      Print it like this

      Print landscape on A4 or Letter at 100% — the Yy card keeps its full 2000×1414 frame and the star on the yo-yo prints crisply.

      How to teach with this card

      Say “ee” then open fast — ee-yes becomes yes. The glide from ee is exactly what y does; children discover they already own the sound.

      Letter sound

      Y makes the /y/ glide at the start of yo-yo, yes and you — tongue high and forward, sliding straight into the vowel.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Yo-Yo lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Phonics & Beginning Sounds (Class 28) class on the Learning Path.

      Zebra Flashcard — Letter Z for Preschoolers

      Zz beside a striped zebra — /z/ is the buzzing twin of /s/, and zebra closes the set: the last letter, the last sound, and the animal that wears the alphabet’s boldest coat.

      How this card helps

      Zz beside the zebra finishes the alphabet with the buzzing sound — and the stripes give the last card the loudest look in the set.

      How to use this card

      Zip-up parade: zip a real or imaginary jacket slowly while buzzing z-z-z-zip, then say zebra and zoo before the zipper closes.

      What kids learn from it

      That Zz is the buzzing end of the alphabet — the voiced twin of s, and the sound of zebra, zoo and zip.

      Print it like this

      Print landscape on A4 or Letter at 100%; the Zz card keeps its full 2000×1414 frame, and the stripes print boldly even in grayscale.

      How to teach with this card

      End the alphabet properly: say the whole A–Z sound wall once a week. The zebra always gets the biggest cheer — save it for last.

      Letter sound

      Z makes the /z/ sound — the s-hiss with the voice switched on: zebra, zoo, zip, zero.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Zebra lesson on the Learning Path.

      From the Phonics & Beginning Sounds (Class 28) class on the Learning Path.
